headline: Six-sided snowflakes, film nights and a scarf for Mum
teaser: Why has every snowflake got six sides? Where do three teenagers like to watch films? And can Ana find enough money for her mum's present?

articles.title: How Is a Snowflake Made?
articles.dek: Snow falls from the sky, but every snowflake starts with something very, very small. What is it?

sources.name: NOAA: How do snowflakes form? Get the science behind snow
Smithsonian Institution Archives: Wilson A. Bentley, pioneering photographer of snowflakes
Guinness World Records: First photograph of a snowflake

paras: It is a cold winter morning. You look out of the window, and everything is white. The roads, the trees and the cars are covered with snow. But what is snow? How is a snowflake made? Let's find out.

Snowflakes are made high up in the clouds. When it is very cold, a tiny drop of water freezes onto a very small piece of dust or pollen. This makes a tiny ice crystal. Then more water from the air freezes onto the crystal. Slowly, the crystal grows bigger and becomes a snowflake.

Look at a snowflake carefully, and you will see six sides or six arms. Why six? Water is made of very, very small parts. When water freezes, these parts join together in a special pattern. This pattern always has six sides. So every snowflake has six sides too.

The weather in the cloud changes the shape of a snowflake. The temperature is the most important thing. At some temperatures, long, thin crystals like needles are formed. At colder temperatures, flat crystals are formed. Every snowflake falls on a different path to the ground, so no two snowflakes are exactly the same.

The first photo of a single snowflake was taken in 1885. It was taken by Wilson Bentley, a young farmer in Vermont, in the USA. He used a camera with a microscope. It wasn't easy, because snowflakes melt very quickly. In his life, he took photos of more than 5,000 snowflakes.

Ice is clear, so why is snow white? A snowflake has lots of tiny sides, and they reflect the light. Clean snow reflects almost all the light, so it looks white. Fresh snow also takes in sound. That is why a snowy street often feels very quiet. Next time it snows, catch a snowflake on a dark glove and look at it!

articles.title: My Favourite Way to Watch Films
articles.dek: Big screen, small laptop or the family sofa? Three teenagers tell us how they like to watch films.
paras: Do you watch films at the cinema, on TV or on your phone? We asked three teenagers about their favourite way to watch films. Here are their answers.

Sofia, 14: I love going to the cinema because the screen is huge and the sound is amazing. I usually go with my cousin on Saturday afternoon. First we buy popcorn and two cold drinks. Then we find our seats near the middle. After that, we turn off our phones. Tickets are quite expensive, so I can only go once a month. But I always save my pocket money for it!

Omar, 15: I watch most films on my laptop in my bedroom. I like it because I can stop the film and watch the rest later. My favourite films are about space and robots. My little brother wants to watch with me, but he is only six. He gets scared, so I choose funny cartoons when he is there. After that, he goes to bed and I watch my space films!

Mei, 13: Friday is film night in my family. We all sit on the big sofa in the living room and watch a film on TV. My dad makes pizza, and my mum chooses the film. Last Friday it was a very old film in black and white. I didn't want to watch it at first, but it was really good! Then we talked about it for an hour.

So, which is the best way? Sofia loves the big screen, and Omar likes his laptop. Mei thinks films are better with her family. What about you? Where do you watch films, and who do you watch them with? Write and tell us!

grammar.point: Linking words: and, but, so, because
grammar.rule: Linking words join ideas. and adds an idea, but shows a different idea, because gives a reason, and so gives a result. First, then and after that show the order of things.

articles.title: A Present for Mum
articles.dek: Ana has found the perfect scarf for her mum. There is only one problem: the price!
paras: On Saturday, Ana went to Greenhill Shopping Centre with her best friend Ruby. It was her mum's birthday on Sunday, and Ana wanted to buy her a present. She only had twenty pounds. Here are some of the notices and messages from that day.

SIGN in the window of a shoe shop: Are your old boots too small? Come in and try our new winter boots. They are warm and very light. Half price today only! Can't find your size on the shelf? Ask a shop assistant.
Text message from Ana to her dad: Hi Dad, I've found a lovely scarf for Mum. It's very soft and it's her favourite colour, blue. But it costs £25, and I haven't got enough money! Can you help me? Ana

NOTICE at the café: Our café is very busy at lunchtime. If there aren't enough seats, please take your food to the tables near the fountain. Please put your rubbish in the bins. Children under 10 must be with an adult.
Message from Dad to Ana: Sorry, I'm too busy at work to come. But I can send you five pounds on your phone. Buy the scarf, and don't forget to get a card too! Love, Dad
NOTE on the door of the small lift: This lift is too small for prams and big trolleys. Please use the big lift next to the toy shop. It goes to all floors. Thank you!
SIGN in the gift shop: Free gift wrapping on Saturdays! Is your present too big to wrap? No problem. We can put it in a nice bag with a ribbon. Please wait at the desk on the left.

opts: You must pay for gift wrapping.
Big presents can't go in the gift shop.
They can put a big present in a bag.
questions.why: 第7段原文：Is your present too big to wrap? No problem. We can put it in a nice bag with a ribbon.
questions.evidence: We can put it in a nice bag with a ribbon.
optWhy: 原文 Free gift wrapping on Saturdays! 是免费的。
原文说大礼物 No problem，没说不能进店。
正确。原文 too big to wrap? … We can put it in a nice bag = 选项 put a big present in a bag。

steps.t: too big to wrap? No problem → 有办法。
put it in a nice bag = put a big present in a bag。

grammar.rule: Use very + adjective to make it stronger: very soft. Use too + adjective when it is more than you want, so there is a problem: too small. Use enough before a noun (enough money) and after an adjective (big enough).

examples.text: It's very soft and it's her favourite colour, blue.
But it costs £25, and I haven't got enough money!
Sorry, I'm too busy at work to come.
This lift is too small for prams and big trolleys.

items.q: These jeans are ___ long. I can't wear them.
items.why: Long is a problem here, so use too.

items.q: Is this jacket big ___ for you?
items.why: enough comes after the adjective: big enough.

items.q: I can't buy the bag. I haven't got ___ money.
items.why: enough comes before a noun: enough money.

items.q: This T-shirt is ___ cheap – only £3! I'll buy two.
items.why: Cheap is good here, not a problem, so use very.

items.q: Tom can't go to the shops alone. He isn't ___ . He's only seven.
items.why: Put enough after the adjective: old enough.

items.q: The box is ___ to carry. Can you help me?
items.why: Put too before the adjective: too heavy to carry.

mindmap.question: How did Ana get a present for her mum?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the text.
summary.model: Ana wanted to buy a scarf for her mum, but she didn't have enough money. Her dad was too busy to come, so he sent her five pounds.

options.t: Ana went shopping for her mum's birthday present.
options.why: This is why Ana went to the shopping centre.
options.evidence: It was her mum's birthday on Sunday, and Ana wanted to buy her a present.

options.t: Ana found a scarf, but she didn't have enough money.
options.why: This is Ana's problem in her message.
options.evidence: But it costs £25, and I haven't got enough money!

options.t: Dad couldn't come, but he sent Ana five pounds.
options.why: This is how the problem ends.
options.evidence: But I can send you five pounds on your phone.

options.t: The big lift is next to the toy shop.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Please use the big lift next to the toy shop.

options.t: Ruby bought a present for her own mum too.
Dad drove to the shopping centre to help Ana.
options.why: Wrong: Dad was too busy at work to come.
options.evidence: Sorry, I'm too busy at work to come.
